key_insight: The paper shows that the complete electrode model for EIT can be implemented with standard Robin boundary conditions, making current-driven electrode simulations portable across finite element codes.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical, accurate way to model medical EIT electrodes in mainstream FEM software without custom boundary formulations.
method: Solve unit-potential Robin subproblems to build an electrode transadmittance matrix.
Prove equivalence to the conventional augmented CEM formulation, including discrete energy and reference handling.
Validate the approach across multiple FEM packages using matched nodal references and 2D P1 meshes.
evidence_signal: Across five FEM packages, electrode-potential differences from EIDORS stayed below 5×10^-13, and errors versus an exact rational-arithmetic reference were below 1.1×10^-13.
watch_item: The equivalence relies on an invertible Robin matrix and careful consistent treatment of the electrode-current integration and reference potential.
paper_title: Implementing the EIT complete electrode model through Robin boundary conditions
